units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Quick, Ben. One sentence.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What is Antwerp?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A river port in Flanders, on the Scheldt, that has been a big deal for about a thousand years.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That's two sentences.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was one with a comma.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fine. Where does the name come from?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Nobody is certain. But the city has a favorite story, and it involves your hand.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I knew it. I win already.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Not yet. Hold on. The legend says a giant called Druoon Antigoon lived by the river.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Any ship that wanted to pass had to pay him a toll.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And if the captain said no?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The giant cut off his hand.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Wow. Rude.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then a hero called Brabo arrives, beats the giant, cuts off his hand, and throws it into the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Oh no. And that's the name?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: That's the story. The name is said to mean hand throwing.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's a legend, and the real origin is still debated.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: But you'll see the giant's hand around town tomorrow.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Where, exactly?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: On top of the main square's fountain, for one.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll get there.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what's the city like today?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One of the major seaports in the world, and a big city that still feels walkable.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The old center is compact, and it's all within a short stroll of the river.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Good. My shoes will be grateful.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Wear good ones. The old streets are cobbled.
